And Ngumoha made quite the impression, with the youngster arguably England's most dangerous player in the second half.

The pre-tournament friendly was played in sweltering conditions in Florida, with the temperature reaching 32 degrees Celsius as the Three Lions look to use their warmup games to acclimatise.

As a result, goals were perhaps of lesser importance in this game, with England focused instead on coping with the conditions.

Ultimately, Kane's goal was enough to get the Three Lions over the line with the win, as Tuchel's side were unable to build on their lead in the second half, but came away without any injuries despite concerns being raised before the game over the playing surface.

Sports.title: Liverpool star ‘open to anything’ after being blocked from January exit by Arne Slot
Sports.content:
Liverpool star ‘open to anything’ after being blocked from January exit by Arne Slot

Federico Chiesa has revealed he could look to leave Liverpool this summer and will hold talks with Andoni Iraola over his future.

The Italian joined the Reds from Juventus in the summer of 2024 but has struggled to establish himself at Anfield and started just once in the Premier League last season.

5 Federico Chiesa has hinted at a future away from Anfield Credit: Getty

Having found playing time hard to come by under Arne Slot, Chiesa could be handed a lifeline following the Dutchman's sacking.

Andoni Iraola has since been announced as Liverpool's new head coach, meaning the 28-year-old will have a new chance to impress.

With Italy failing to qualify for this summer's World Cup, Chiesa will report for Liverpool's pre-season tour of the USA next month, looking to convince Iraola of his value.

But the winger has admitted he will seek talks with the Spaniard first before deciding on his future as he targets increased playing time.

'Barely played'

Speaking to Italian publication La Gazzetta dello Sport about his upcoming plans, Chiesa said: "I want to play.

“If I don't find consistency in the Premier League, I'll have to look elsewhere. I barely played in my first year at Liverpool, and in the last one, very little.

“I'll go on a training camp in the US, then I'll talk to the club and the new manager, Iraola, and we'll see."

Chiesa also revealed that he had a January exit blocked by Liverpool due to Alexander Isak's injury and Mohamed Salah's participation at the Africa Cup of Nations.

The ex-Juventus star continued: "I've played very little since the start of 2026. I have a great relationship with Liverpool.

“In January, the club and Slot told me I couldn't leave; they needed me, partly for numerical reasons. We were in a tight spot.

5 Iraola was confirmed as the new Liverpool manager just days after Slot's sacking Credit: Getty

5 This could hand Chiesa a chance to revive his Liverpool career Credit: Getty

"I understood the situation and I stayed with a smile.

"People are always talking about Liverpool - last year they helped me win the Premier League."

Among the clubs touted as potential next destinations for Chiesa are former side Juventus, while he has also been linked with Cesc Fabregas' Como, who recently qualified for the Champions League.

And the wideman refused to rule out a move to either side as he insisted game time is his priority next season.

Chiesa said: "I'm open to anything; the important thing is to play.

“I'm not so presumptuous as to say: I have to be a starter. I'm ready to fight for a place, anywhere.”

5 Chiesa scored 32 goals in 131 games for Juventus over a four-year spell Credit: Getty

"Fabregas is a top coach; no one would have ever imagined Como like this: a beautiful team to watch, too."

As for Juventus, where he previously starred between 2020 and 2024, Chiesa admitted he would welcome a return to Turin.

He said: “I'd like to return to the Bianconeri.

"I would never have left. It was also said that I wanted a lot of money, but the truth is different: I was never offered a renewal. We never even discussed it.

After explaining the circumstances of his 2024 exit, he added: "But Juventus is always in my heart, and I'd like to return."

Chiesa's Liverpool career

Chiesa joined Liverpool in August 2024 in a deal worth up to £12.5million, and was the first signing of the Arne Slot era.

5 Chiesa's only two Premier League goals have come against Bournemouth and Crystal Palace

But his time in Merseyside hasn't gone to plan, having made 50 appearances in all competitions, with just nine starts.

During this time, the forward has scored five goals altogether, two of them in the Premier League, including a late winner against Bournemouth on the opening day of the 2025/26 season.

Despite this, he has endeared himself to supporters with his high-energy cameos off the bench and tasted Premier League glory in his debut season at Anfield.

Sports.title: Anthony Martial becomes free agent as ex-Manchester United star rips up deal with club after 20 games
Sports.content:
Anthony Martial becomes free agent as ex-Manchester United star rips up deal with club after 20 games

Anthony Martial has reportedly reached an agreement to leave Monterrey one year early.

The former Manchester United forward joined the Mexican side last September on a two-year deal through to 2027, with the option of an extra 12 months.

2 Martial arrived at Monterrey with plenty of high hopes Credit: AFP

However, journalist Fabrizio Romano reports both parties have agreed to end the partnership ahead of schedule.

Martial departs Monterrey having played just 20 games for the club, where he scored just once and provided three assists.

His time with Monterrey was disrupted by a dislocated shoulder, which he sustained in February during a clash against Club Leon.

Martial had to be taken off in a stretcher, such was his discomfort.

The 30-year-old's final appearance came on March 18 in the second leg of Monterrey's CONCACAF Champions Cup round of 16 clash against Cruz Azul, which they ultimately lost 4-3 on aggregate.

On the road again

Martial's exit from Monterrey means he is now on the hunt for his third club since leaving United in 2024.

Prior to joining the Mexican side, where he played alongside Sergio Ramos, Martial was on the books at AEK Athens.

The forward moved to the Greek outfit on a three-year deal but departed after just one season having scored nine goals in 23 appearances across all competitions.

Martial's exit from Monterrey is a far cry from where he was less than a decade ago.

Martial's alarming decline over the years

It was in 2015 when United forked out £36million to sign Martial from Monaco, a figure that constituted the highest fee paid for a teenager.

2 Martial won the Golden Boy award in 2015, heralding him as a star of the future Credit: Getty

He made an instant impression when he scored on debut during a 3-1 win over Liverpool, giving Red Devils supporters hope they had a serious star on their hands.

However, aside from an impressive 2019/20 campaign where he netted 23 times across all competitions, Martial struggled to live up to the hype.

The 30-cap France international ultimately departed United upon the expiry of his contract in May 2024 having made over 300 appearances for the club.

"After nine incredible years at the club, the time has come for me to turn a new page in my career," Martial said when confirming he would leave Old Trafford for good.

"Since I arrived in 2015, I have had the immense honour of wearing this shirt and playing in front of you, the best supporters in the world!

"You have been an unwavering support, through the good times and the difficult. Your passion and loyalty have been a constant source of motivation for me.

"I'd like to thank you from the bottom of my heart for everything you've done for me. Your songs, your encouragement and your love for the club are memories that will remain engraved in my heart forever."

Sports.title: Rafael Leao sent off in World Cup warm-up to leave Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal sweating
Sports.content:
Rafael Leao sent off in World Cup warm-up to leave Cristiano Ronaldo and Portugal sweating

Portugal's World Cup preparations took a huge blow as Rafael Leao was sent off in their friendly with Chile.

The nation, captained by Cristiano Ronaldo, were at full-strength going into the clash.



3 Faundez's tackle on Leao kick-started a chain of events that led to two red cards Credit: Getty

That saw Leao start on the left-wing to service his 41-year-old teammate.

However, manager Roberto Martinez's best laid plans went awry in first-half stoppage time.

Chilean star Felipe Faundez went in hard on the winger before then going into another challenge with Portugal full-back Joao Cancelo.



Faundez cleared the ball but clashed with Cancelo as he rolled off the pitch.

The incident saw Ivan Roman barrel in to protect Faundez, with Leao then evening the scores.



However, Leao and Roman then traded pushes before one from the AC Milan ace finally put his 19-year-old rival on his backside.

Teammates swarmed while Roman lay on the turf holding his face, almost in tears.



Both stars, though, were sent off by referee Luca Zufferli in Lisbon.

Will Rafael Leao be suspended for the World Cup?

Ordinarily, Leao might expect a three-game ban.

That would see him miss a friendly with Nigeria on June 10 and their opening two matches against DR Congo and Uzbekistan.

3 Leao only managed 12 goal contributions for AC Milan in Serie A last year Credit: Getty

However, FIFA has a recent history of making these bans shorter, with a portion of the ban suspended.

Ronaldo himself is able to play at the World Cup despite being sent off in similar circumstances against Republic of Ireland in November.



He struck Dara O'Shea with his elbow in the defeat earning a straight red card.

In the end, though, he missed just one game - against Armenia, and then had the other two matches suspended.

A FIFA statement read: "If Cristiano Ronaldo commits another infringement of a similar nature and gravity during the probationary period, the suspension set out in the disciplinary decision shall be deemed automatically revoked and the remaining two matches must be served immediately."

This leniency will also see ex-Brighton star Jurgen Locadia available for the World Cup.



3 Ronaldo was hit with a red card in Dublin but had his suspension reduced Credit: Getty

He was given a straight red against Scotland that could have seen him banned for two matches.

However, FIFA reduced this to one, meaning he only misses their friendly with Aruba ahead of their tournament debut.

Are Chile at the World Cup?

Leao's foe Roman, who plays his club football for Atletico Mineiro, doesn't have the same worry.



Chile failed to reach the 48-team tournament, and that's despite CONMEBOL having six qualifying places and a play-off place.

In the end, though, Nicolas Cordova's men finished bottom of the table, winning just two games.

Chile have now not reached a World Cup since 2014.

Sports.title: Robert Lewandowski tipped for free transfer to Premier League giants this summer
Sports.content:
Robert Lewandowski tipped for free transfer to Premier League giants this summer

Manchester United have been urged to make a move for Robert Lewandowski this summer by former striker Giuseppe Rossi.

The 37-year-old will officially be a free agent next month after running down his Barcelona contract.



4 Robert Lewandowski leaves Barcelona as one of their all-time top goalscorers Credit: Getty

Lewandowski will depart the Camp Nou after four years, having joined Barca from Bayern Munich in 2022.

One of Europe's deadliest strikers in the 21st century, the Pole has only cemented his reputation in Spain.

He leaves Barca having scored 120 goals in 193 games, winning three league titles, three Spanish Super Cups and the Copa del Rey.



'No brainer'

Despite being in his late thirties, Lewandowski's continued prolific goalscoring will put him on the radar of plenty of top clubs this summer.

There is also strong interest from beyond Europe, with several Saudi Pro League sides and MLS outfit Chicago Fire all keen to sign him.



But ex-Italy international Rossi, who spent three years at Old Trafford between 2004 and 2007, has urged Man United to consider pursuing him, insisting his presence would benefit young striker Benjamin Sesko.

Speaking to Ozoon ahead of the World Cup, Rossi said: "Robert Lewandowski to Man United? Yeah, why not?"



“Of course, Lewandowski would be an incredible asset for the young players, providing his experience and big-game knowledge.

"With Benjamin Sesko being a young, growing player, having someone like Lewandowski on the team would only benefit him.

"It's a no-brainer. He has a huge resume and on a short-term deal, it’s a win-win."

Sesko joined Man United from RB Leipzig last summer in a £74m deal and initially struggled to make his mark in the Premier League.



4 Nine of Benjamin Sesko's 11 goals this term came in the second half of the season Credit: Getty

4 Lewandowski will leave Barcelona after clinching the 14th league title of his career Credit: Getty

But the Slovenian found his feet in the second half of the season, ultimately finishing the campaign with 11 league goals.

It's fair to say Lewandowski could teach him a thing or two about the art of goalscoring, having fired in over 650 goals in his illustrious career.



Last season, the Pole scored 14 goals in 31 league games for Barcelona as they tasted LaLiga glory, despite starting on just 17 occasions.

In fact, Rossi isn't the only ex-United man to highlight Lewandowski as a potential mentor figure for Sesko, with Red Devils legend Rio Ferdinand making a similar argument recently.

After Lewandowski announced his departure from Barcelona, Ferdinand reacted on social media: “What a guy, what a player!!

“Experienced option next season in UCL & help with development of Sesko?”



4 Michael Carrick's United will have a much busier calendar next season after securing European football Credit: Getty

Having secured a third-place Premier League finish and a return to the Champions League, United will be looking to strengthen in the summer as they aim to compete on all fronts under newly-appointed permanent boss Michael Carrick.

Lewandowski's Barcelona career

In four years at Barcelona, Lewandowski fired in a staggering 120 goals and provided a further 24 assists.

83 of his goals came in LaLiga, with his best tally coming last term as he netted 27 times in 34 league games.



In the Champions League, Lewandowski scored 23 goals in 38 appearances, reaching the 100-goal milestone in the competition whilst playing for the club.

As for trophies, the Polish superstar has collected another seven during his stint in Catalonia, taking his over career haul to a huge 33, having won a huge 10 Bundesliga titles with Borussia Dortmund and Bayern respectively.

Sports.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel unhappy with his side's first-half showing - and criticises players for not sticking to the gameplan against New Zealand
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel criticised England's first half XI – and the pitch – as the Three Lions started their World Cup preparations with a low key victory over New Zealand.

The German appeared less than impressed with an opening 45 minutes which saw Harry Kane score the only goal of the game, and accused his starters of going 'freestyle'.

'I'm OK,' he said. 'Not super happy. In the first half we were out of position and it was a bit too much freestyle.'

When asked what he meant by that, Tuchel suggested his side had gone rogue and ditched the gameplan. 'We were changing positions for too long,' he said. 'It's not a problem to change positions, but you have to find the position again, so that everyone knows how to start the attack, and then we can just accelerate the game easier.

'And we were taking crosses, a lot of crosses, long-range shots, which is normally not our style of play. We played a lot of long balls, we played a lot of long passes - that was not part of training in the last four days.'

On Friday, Daily Mail Sport revealed how England were to face a 'plug and play' pitch that had only been laid around a week ago at the Raymond James Stadium, home of the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

And Tuchel was far from impressed with the surface, despite his side coming through with no injuries.

'It was very difficult to play on,' he said. 'We have no injuries and there were no concerns, but it was very uneven and to move the ball quickly, when you have the ball for the majority of the match, it doesn't help you.'

Thomas Tuchel was not pleased with England's first-half display against New Zealand

When asked if he was surprised he had to deal with that in the first outing, he responded: 'It is what it is. It can happen, I know it from pre-season tours overseas, that this can happen if you play in stadiums, normally in football stadiums, that the pitch is maybe too new, and not fully grown and not fully even.'

Tuchel started with Morgan Rogers in the side, which prompted some to wonder whether Jude Bellingham may have to be content with a place on the bench when the tournament starts. However, Bellingham was made captain when he arrived for the second half - and Tuchel warned not to read too much into the situation.

'Decisions are not made yet for Croatia, and there were no hidden messages,' Tuchel said. 'We try to have more or less equal teams, and Harry and Morgan played many matches for us together, and we had yesterday a strong group in training with Jude, Nico O'Reilly and Elliot Anderson, and we just kept them together because they enjoyed playing against us yesterday in training. So that was it, no secret messages.'

Tuchel went on to praise the Real Madrid playmaker, who missed two months of the season with a hamstring injury. 'He comes from an injury and is full of energy, and happy to be back on the pitch,' he said.

'He had his break, unfortunately, in a decisive part of the season, Champions League season, and then a national campaign for the championship in Spain, so this was very unfortunate for Real Madrid and for him personally, but you can see now that he is actually in a sweet spot, he comes back, he's fresh, he wants to play, and he's in top shape.'

Meanwhile, All Whites coach Darren Bazeley, the former Watford, Wolves and England Under 21 defender, also appeared a tad unimpressed with England's performance. 'If they want to win the World Cup they need to be better than they were today,' he said.

Sports.title: Iran told to leave US within 24 hours of World Cup matches as coaching staff visas are denied
Sports.content:
Iran have been told they must enter and leave US soil on the same day of matches while ‘integral’ members of their coaching staff have been denied visas to the World Cup.

The country’s ambassador to Mexico, where the squad is staying thanks to the ongoing conflict with the US, said on Saturday that their players would have to be in and out of the US within 24 hours.

Iran – whose group matches are in Los Angeles and Seattle – were due to stay in Tucson, Arizona but will now fly in.

Iranian national team depart Turkey for training base in Mexico ahead of 2026 FIFA World Cup

‘We can enter in the morning and we must leave the same day,’ Iran's envoy Abolfazl Pasandideh told reporters.

US officials said visas have been issued to all players and ‘necessary support staff’ ahead of their June 16 opener.

They added that Iran would not be allowed to ‘abuse this system to sneak terrorists into the United States under false pretences’.

United States president Donald Trump with FIFA top brass Gianni Infantino

However, Iran’s embassy in Turkey said visas had been denied to ‘a large portion of the managerial and executive staff’ and accused the Americans of ‘politically biased interference in sport’. They claimed visas had been denied to a ‘large portion of the managerial and executive staff’ and ‘technical advisers’.

Iranian state media claimed the head of the football federation and his deputy were among those denied entry.

Iran open their World Cup account against New Zealand in California on June 16, before facing Belgium and Egypt in California and Seattle, respectively.

Sports.title: England pass test of coping with the US heat and avoiding injury on poor pitch will allow fans to dream of World Cup glory again, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
The England fans sat in the Florida sun, blinking back the sweltering heat and feeling the dream beginning to stir again. It is the dream England always dreams. The dream which, for the last 60 years, has always been dashed.

Thomas Tuchel made 11 changes at half time and there were moments where this victory over New Zealand felt like a training game. But the refrain of Three Lions began to boom around the Raymond James Stadium. Jules Rimet is still gleaming. England supporters danced in the stands.

If this game represented anything, it represented the beginning of hope. Because however much we try to quell it, the hope always takes hold. There are 11 days until England’s opening game of the World Cup against Croatia in Dallas but there is enough talent in this squad to let the hope flourish and to clutch at the tentative signs of encouragement on view here.

Harry Kane played, Harry Kane scored and Harry Kane was not injured. That was the best news because without Kane, there probably is no hope. Him staying healthy was more important than him scoring the 79th goal of his England career in his 113th appearance.

Harry Kane opens his account on US soil, scoring his 67th goal of the season

There is enough talent in this squad to let the hope flourish and to clutch at the tentative signs of encouragement on view here

Thomas Tuchel made 11 changes at half time and there were moments where this victory over New Zealand felt like a training game

Other small victories? Well, England survived the pitch at the stadium the locals call the Ray-Jay. It was supposed to be full of potholes and pitfalls but England negotiated them without alarm.

England have never before played in a stadium where a pirate ship sits behind one of the goals. The cannon that booms out from it every time the Tampa Bay Buccaneers score a touchdown stayed silent, even when Kane scored. This was a day for quieter satisfactions.

Jordan Henderson played well, especially for a player who keeps being told he should be on the coaching staff, not on the pitch. Morgan Rogers started ahead of Jude Bellingham but when Bellingham came on in the second half, he was given the captain’s armband. Decipher that puzzle if you can.

Morgan Rogers started ahead of Jude Bellingham but it is unclear who will start as the No10

When Bellingham came on in the second half, he was given the captain’s armband - decipher that puzzle if you can

Marcus Rashford was England’s best player in the first half. Bellingham looked a class above in the second half. He often does. Logic says he is simply too good not to start against Croatia on June 17th.

But then this was all against a side that had just lost 4-0 to Haiti in Miami. This was an exercise in coping with the heat. It was a start. Nothing more. England play Costa Rica in another friendly in Orlando on Wednesday and then, a couple of days later, head to their training base in Kansas City. This will be a World Cup that builds slowly.

It was hard to read too much into a team selection for a match against poor opponents on a bad pitch but it was also hard not to read too much into the selection of Morgan Rogers at number 10 behind Kane.

It was hard to read too much into Thomas Tuchel's team selection for a match against poor opponents on a bad pitch

The battle between Rogers and Bellingham for the crucial creative starting berth in the team is the story that will run and run all the way to England’s opening game. Rogers’ selection for this match and the general preference that Tuchel has shown for him over Bellingham suggests that he has his nose ahead in the struggle with his friend. It will be a big call to leave out a Real Madrid starter from the England line-up.

Some were surprised that Kane started, given his importance to the side but then there is only so long he can be protected. If there is an excess of caution among the fans about wrapping him in cotton wool, it is because everyone knows he is the one player who cannot be replaced.

England started well enough but it was the 14th minute before they carved out their first clear chance. The inclusion of Jordan Henderson has been mocked by many. Some have suggested he is only in the squad to keep Bellingham happy. But he was the best player on the pitch in the opening stages.

It was his brilliant, driven pass down the inside right channel that played in Ollie Watkins but as Watkins bore down on goal, he mishit his shot and it flew wildly across the face of goal. Kane hit a sweeter shot from 35 yards a minute later but it was too close to Max Crocombe and he beat it away with his fists.

England did not have it all their own way. Midway through the half, Matt Garbett stepped outside his man and hit a curling, dipping shot that bounced just in front of Jordan Pickford. Pickford dealt with it well, and pushed it away to safety but it was a reminder that New Zealand did not intend to be sacrificial lambs.

Henderson prompted another attack that ended with Kobbie Mainoo bending a shot just over the bar. Ten minutes before half-time, a Kane back-post header brought a fine finger-tip save out of Crocombe.

The breakthrough came on the stroke of the interval. Djed Spence curled a cross in from the left and Kane rose to steer a deft glancing header across goal and into the far corner. It was a beautiful goal from a striker who cannot stop scoring. Crocombe had no chance this time.

Djed Spence curled a cross in from the left and Kane rose to steer a deft glancing header across goal and into the far corner

Tuchel made 11 changes at half-time. Bellingham, Ivan Toney, and Anthony Gordon were among those who came on. Rio Ngumoha was brought on for his England debut. Dan Burn, another introduction, hit the post four minutes into his appearance after Crocombe came for a high ball and got nowhere near it.

Bellingham’s first contribution was a Rolls Royce pass with the outside of his right foot to Gordon. Soon after, he played a neat ball into Toney, who was tripped in the area. The referee pointed to the spot but Toney had strayed offside.

In a break in the game, the television cameras picked out a woman in the crowd holding up a sign that said ‘Phil Foden should be here’. More will feel that Cole Palmer should be here. But the die is cast now. This is still an England squad rich in talent.

They could not add to Kane’s goal in the second half but that did not matter. It was a game to be negotiated. It was a match in which to suffer in the heat and know that it was money in the bank for far, far tougher tests that lie ahead when the World Cup starts and the singing of Three Lions grows in volume.

Sports.title: USA's World Cup send-off ends in loss to Germany as familiar frailties haunt Mauricio Pochettino's team... despite Antonee Robinson's stunner
Sports.content:
They brought out Chance the Rapper and performing dogs and US soccer stars of yesteryear. They let off fireworks and flew B52s over the stands of Soldier Field. But nothing stirs a sold-out crowd or lights the World Cup fuse quite like a thunderbolt and a scrap.

Mauricio Pochettino’s team provided both in this send-off against Germany that answered many questions about the grit and quality of this US team but posed several more heading into a momentous summer.

After Kai Havertz’s early opener threatened to suck the life out of Soldier Field, the USMNT rallied before Antonee Robinson levelled the game with an outrageous, thunderous volley.

That brought 63,000 fans to their feet then, in stoppage time, substitute Tim Weah’s hefty tackle on David Raum sparked a mass shoving match and cries of ‘U-S-A’ from this Chicago crowd.

There was only one issue. In between those flashpoints, Leroy Sane had placed a shot into the bottom corner to condemn the US to defeat in this World Cup dress rehearsal.

Once again, there were more than enough shoots of optimism to suggest Pochettino's team can go deep this summer - their resilience after going behind, their attacking invention and the performance of Christian Pulisic. But also enough lingering fragility to temper expectations heading into next week's opener against Paraguay.

This 2-1 loss was America's ninth consecutive defeat against European opposition dating back to the 2022 World Cup. And that will sting for Pochettino and his players.

Germany beat the United States in their final World Cup warm-up game in Chicago on Saturday

Christian Pulisic and Co were beaten 2-1 at Soldier Field ahead of this summer's tournament

Antonee Robinson scored a stunning volley to level the match shortly before halftime

Because this more than a final warm-up game. This was more than a send-off match sponsored by Coca-Cola. This friendly, against the four-time world champions, the No 10-ranked team in the world, was another chance to prove how good the US can be under Pochettino. To show that they can mix it with the best teams in the world.

Once more, the USA demonstrated that they can hurt anyone. They created ample chances. But once more this team was undone by soft goals. And that is the nagging concern heading into next week. What needs to change for this skid to end?

Many of the American heroes of 1994 were paraded on the pitch shortly before kick-off. Hairlines have receded and waistlines have expanded since their heroics three decades ago. But the legacy of the last home World Cup lives on in this generation and after Pochettino’s players emerged from the tunnel to warm up, they locked arms with their forefathers for a group photo. A journey spanning 32 years captured in a single picture.

Alexi Lalas and Co were decked out in the same red and white stripes that the USMNT will wear this summer. So were thousands of fans in the streets of downtown Chicago and on the walk to Soldier Field.

Make no mistake, however, the battle for hearts and minds is not won: as soccer fans wandered through Grant Park, hordes of people headed in the other direction… toward Pokemon Go Fest. At one point, a group debating the qualities of Matt Freese were passed by a couple discussing the possible whereabouts of Pikachu.

There is plenty of work to be done on the pitch, too. That much became obvious after just 106 seconds, when Joshua Kimmich clipped a free-kick toward the back post, where Havertz was waiting. All alone.

The Arsenal forward had drifted off the back of Tim Ream and away from Miles Robinson. It was clever from Havertz and from Nico Schlotterbeck, who acted as a blocker to buy his teammate space. From an American point of view, however, it was painfully soft. Just like Senegal’s two goals last week.

Mauricio Pochettino's team will kick off their World Cup campaign against Paraguay next week

Germany winger Leroy Sane (right) scored the winning goal during the second half in Chicago

The early setback silenced Soldier Field and, for a few minutes, the US were teetering. Havertz had the ball in the net once more, only for the US to be saved by the assistant’s flag. All of a sudden, the specter of Chris Richards loomed large. Without him, Pochettino had played a back four that - at times - looked brittle. They need the Crystal Palace defender back.

By half-time, however, Pochettino’s team was level and in the ascendancy. Folarin Balogun flashed a teasing ball across goal; Alex Freeman carried the ball well from right back; Sergino Dest fired over from inside the box.

And after ending his goal drought against Senegal, Pulisic seems to be coming to the boil at the perfect time. The winger had a couple of promising openings here including when he sent two defenders the wrong way, only for his shot to fly over the bar.

Thankfully Robinson’s volley soared the right side of the woodwork. It came after a USMNT corner was headed clear. The ball looped into the sky and landed on his left foot. It was a thunderous strike that gave goalkeeper Oliver Baumann no chance. And just like that, the US were level and momentum - kickstarted against Senegal last week - began to snowball.

It was a goal worthy of winning any game, a volley that set off flares and sparked renewed hope.

Unfortunately, 10 minutes into the second half, both Havertz and Jamal Musiala were allowed too much time around the box. They combined before Sane rolled a shot past Freese to ensure Robinson's volley was merely the highlight in another defeat.

Sports.title: Simone Biles reveals terrifying health scare and says she 'almost died' in hospital this week
Sports.content:
Simone Biles reveals terrifying health scare and says she 'almost died' in hospital this week

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Simone Biles has claimed she 'almost died' this week after suffering a horrifying health scare and being rushed to hospital.

The Olympic legend, 29, has given no further details on her condition, but she revealed the scary incident on Instagram on Saturday afternoon.

In a post on her story, alongside a photo of her wearing several hospital wristbands, she wrote: 'I'm not one to normally share things like this because I value privacy in today's age.

'But almost dying wasn't on my bingo card earlier this week. This was one of, if not the scariest experience of my life, especially since Jonathan was in Indy for practices.

'I've been in bed resting this week, I'll explain sooner or later but s/o to my close circle who reached out, checked in, visited & or sent flowers.'

In a further post, she shared a photo of herself lying in bed with her dogs, alongside the caption 'I'll be here' and a screenshot of an extremely elevated resting heartbeat.

Simone Biles, pictured in December, suffered a terrifying health scare earlier this week

Biles shared the news on her Instagram story, telling her followers she 'almost died' this week

It is not clear what caused Biles to be rushed to hospital, but it appears she is now back home after the serious health scare. On Friday afternoon, she shared pictures from a visit to watch the MLB team St. Louis Cardinals with husband Owens, who threw out the first pitch for his hometown team.

Owens shared her post on his Instagram story, joking that Biles is 'from the crib now' - comments that perhaps indicate the scariest part of the ordeal is now behind the couple.

But the news of her scare led to an outpouring of support for the 11-time Olympic medalist, who has not competed since the 2024 Games in Paris, where she won three golds.

Biles currently lives in Texas with her NFL husband Jonathan Owens, who recently signed a one-year, $1.4million deal with the Indianapolis Colts after two years in Chicago with the Bears.

The loved-up pair have built their dream lakeside home from scratch, but Owens was not present for Biles' health scare given his NFL commitments in the Midwest.

Biles and Owens met in 2020 on the celebrity dating app Raya, in the middle of the coronavirus lockdown.

Owens previously opened up on their first few months of dating in an interview with Texas Monthly, noting: 'It was one of the few times in her life where everything was just shut off and she couldn’t do anything.

'We used it to get to know each other... really get to know each other. It created our bond and made it stronger. Now, I'm so thankful.'

Biles, 29, on the red carpet in Madrid, Spain at the Laureus World Sports Awards in April

Biles pictured alongside her husband Jonathan Owens, who plays for the Indianapolis Colts

The pair tied the knot in 2023 and have since been each other's biggest supporters, regularly attending each other's NFL games and gymnastics competitions.

Biles, 29, is widely considered the greatest gymnast of all time and is America's most decorated gymnast in Olympic history.

She has not ruled out competing again at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 due to it being a home Games, but gymansts do not typically compete that late into their career.

Just last week, before her health scare, Biles said she is torn over the decision.

'I'd say we’re still at about 50 per cent,' she said to French publication El Pais.

'Although I’ll also take this opportunity to say one thing: I feel we should know how to admire athletes while they are active and competing.

Last week, Biles said she was still unsure if she would compete at the LA Olympics in 2028

'I've already been to three Olympic Games, and I feel fulfilled. It’s crazy to see how people always want more and more from you. In the end, the decision will always be mine.

'I feel our bodies are a bit like an hourglass that’s slowly running out. Right now, I’m 29, and although longevity in the elite has advanced by leaps and bounds, it would be a huge sacrifice to try to be at Los Angeles [at 31]. We’ll have to see.'

She added that since the Paris Games, she has mainly stayed active by doing pilates with husband Owens, explaining: 'Honestly it’s not fun at all. It’s very hard, pure pain and effort. But he loves it. And I do it because I love sharing it with him.'

Sports.title: England 1-0 New Zealand PLAYER RATINGS: Who was 'easily' the Three Lions' best performer? Why did one player give fans reason to 'worry'? And which star 'looked isolated'?
Sports.content:
England played the first of two friendlies in preparation for the World Cup on Saturday night, beating New Zealand 1-0 in Tampa, Florida.

Thomas Tuchel put out two separate teams for the game - each playing 45 minutes on a poor pitch - and the match proved to be a decent run out for 22 of the players currently in the England camp.

But who was the Three Lions' best player? Who caused reason for worry? And who 'looked isolated'?

England will take on Costa Rica on Wednesday in their second and final warm-up game for the competition, before taking on Croatia in their curtain-raiser a week later.

In these two games, fringe players will have been hoping to convince Tuchel they can play a key part in their side's journey, with the likely starters keen to nail down their places.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was at the Raymond James Stadium to rate the players.

England played their first of two friendly games prior to the World Cup on Saturday evening

Harry Kane scored the only goal as two separate Three Lions sides played a half each

First-half

Jordan Pickford - 6

Made the one big save asked of him when ball bounced wickedly in goalmouth. Kicking can be better though, in terms of accuracy and ability to penetrate.

Jarrell Quansah - 5

An early scare when New Zealand got in behind and, like Spence on opposite flank, you'd worry about them against top wingers.

Marc Guehi - 6

Loose in possession once early on and led to chance. Later did well to deny Wood a run on goal but can do better on whole.

John Stones - 6.5

A bit of a stroll and, most importantly, came through it with no fitness concerns. Looked comfortable in what he had to do.

John Stones looked comfortable and made it through the game with no injury concerns

Djed Spence - 7

Questions over defending were obvious early on but he recovered and delivered teasing cross for Kane goal in stoppage-time.

Jordan Henderson - 7

Completed 48 of 49 passes, including one delicious ball to send Watkins clear. Seized responsibility early on. Looked good.

Kobbie Mainoo - 6

Did fine but there were a few loose balls and didn't do enough to raise possibility of him starting tournament.

Ollie Watkins - 6.5

Less familiar right-wing role and spooned a big chance when clear. Came into game as half wore on and was lively.

Morgan Rogers - 5.5

Significantly given nod behind Kane but didn't really do enough to impress, despite seeing plenty of ball.

Marcus Rashford - 8

Easily England's best. Looked lean and keen. Came close with 25-yard dipper and created five chances.

Harry Kane - 7

Too deep at times, which was one big complaint of Euro 2024. Scored with only second touch in box, but that's what matters.

Marcus Rashford was England's best player and came close with one long-range effort

Second-half

James Trafford - 6

A spectator and had no saves to make in his 45 minutes. Did fine with his feet and on one occasion dashing from his goal to claim.

Reece James - 6

Looked strong and steady both physically and in possession and that's all that can be asked of likely starting right back.

Ezri Konsa - 6

New Zealand's only getaway of half came in behind Villa defender, but was hardly tested apart from that.

Dan Burn - 7

Denied first England goal when header clipped post, but that effort proved his nuisance value in box. Good on ball.

Tino Livramento - 6

Hard to judge defensive contribution because opposition barely attacked second-half. Tidy on ball in first action since April.

Elliot Anderson showed determination to make things happen without really getting anywhere

Elliot Anderson - 6.5

Showed usual determination to get on ball and make things happen - most passes into final third - even if endeavour did not really lead anywhere.

Nico O'Reilly - 6

Used in midfield - will likely start versus Croatia at left back - but was not involved enough for a player of his talent.

Rio Ngumoha - 6.5

Became England's fifth youngest debutant. One or two moments of trickery and livened the crowd in what was largely dull affair.

Jude Bellingham - 7

Immediately showed class with probing balls and looked to take initiative wearing armband. A better showing than Rogers.

Anthony Gordon - 6

Not as impactful as Rashford but was unlucky when one dribble led to blocked shot. Seemed to tire a little after lack of action at Newcastle.

Antony Gordon did not have as much impact as Rashford - his direct competitor for a starting spot on the left

Ivan Toney - 5

Not involved enough and looked isolated. Won penalty only to be ruled offside, and just about summed up his half.

MANAGER

Thomas Tuchel - 6.5

Will have learnt that Rashford deserves to start but will leave with doubts over best starter at No 10. Performance was too slow, and team will need to quicken when real action starts.

Sports.title: Man United target and Portugal star is sent off for striking opponent in the face during friendly on eve of the World Cup
Sports.content:
Portugal forward Rafael Leao - who has been of interest to Manchester United - was sent off in a pre-World Cup friendly for striking an opponent in the face.

The 48 teams that will compete in the summer's tournament are playing friendly matches in preparation, and Portugal, who are among the favourites to go all the way in North America, took on Chile on Saturday night.

Roberto Martinez's side, led by captain Cristiano Ronaldo, secured victory, winning 2-1 thanks to goals from Bruno Fernandes and Goncalo Guedes.

But what grabbed attention was an incident at the end of the first-half, that saw Leao and Chile star Ivan Roman both given their marching orders.

Footage showed the duo clashing on the side of the pitch following an incident between Portugal's Joao Cancelo and Chile's Felipe Faundez, with the latter appearing to kick out at his opponent.

That led to a scuffle, with Roman centre stage before Leao went steaming in.

Rafael Leao (second left) was sent off in a friendly after striking an opponent on the eve of the World Cup

The forward is keen on a move to the Premier League after revealing he is looking to leave AC Milan this summer

After Roman appeared to push his head toward Cancelo, Leao pushed him twice in the chest before appearing to do so again in the throat.

After Roman pushed back, Leao then appeared to throw a strike of sorts, which seemingly connected with his rival's jaw.

Roman carried on confronting Leao, and then, after receiving what seemed to be another push, hit the deck.

Both players were sent off, and it remains to be seen whether Leao could face retrospective action that could impact his World Cup participation.

His fist was open, though - which could benefit him in terms of any future charge.

Leao, who United have monitored for some time now, has revealed he is keen to leave current club AC Milan, with the Premier League his preferred destination.

His contract runs until 2028, and he is expected to play a key role for Portugal this summer alongside the likes of Champions League-winning duo Joao Neves and Vitinha.

Sports.title: Ruben Loftus-Cheek gives Man United supporters an insight into incoming £39m star Ederson after going up against Atalanta star in Serie A
Sports.content:
Ruben Loftus-Cheek gives Man United supporters an insight into incoming £39m star Ederson after going up against Atalanta star in Serie A

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ruben Loftus-Cheek has backed Ederson to succeed at Manchester United ahead of his impending arrival from Atalanta.

Ederson, 26, will officially put pen to paper at Old Trafford in early July when FIFA's international transfer clearing system opens after agreeing a £39million move.

The Brazilian is Michael Carrick's first signing since becoming permanent United boss, replacing his compatriot Casemiro, whose contract expired. Manuel Ugarte is also expected to leave the Red Devils this summer.

Ederson, a versatile midfielder capable of playing as a No6 or box-to-box No8, has made 138 appearances for Italian side Atalanta, scoring 13 goals.

"He's quick, strong, good on the ball...he's a good signing" 👀



Ruben Loftus-Cheek gave a glowing endorsement of potential Manchester United signing Ederson 💪 pic.twitter.com/xagEA9yhKd — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) June 6, 2026

Ederson, 26, will officially put pen to paper at Old Trafford in early July when FIFA's international transfer clearing system opens after agreeing a £39million move

Loftus-Cheek last faced Ederson on May 10 and United's new man came out on top, scoring and assisting as Atalanta beat AC Milan 3-2

One man who has had a closer look at Ederson than most is former Chelsea midfielder Loftus-Cheek, who has been plying his trade at AC Milan.

Loftus-Cheek last faced Ederson on May 10 and United's new man came out on top, scoring and assisting as Atalanta beat AC Milan 3-2.

And now he has given United supporters a taste of what to expect from their maiden summer signing.

Speaking to Sky Sports at the Monaco Grand Prix, Cheek said: 'He'll do just fine. The times we've played against each other, he's been very physical. He's quick, he's strong, he's good on the ball. I think he'll do really well – he's a good signing.'

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa’s Liverpool escape hopes dealt damaging blow by club chief
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa’s Liverpool escape hopes dealt damaging blow by club chief

Federico Chiesa is expected to leave Liverpool this summer after a couple of difficult seasons at Anfield but a move away from the club might not be as straight-forward as first thought

View 2 Images Chiesa has just two years left on his Liverpool deal (Image: Getty Images)

Federico Chiesa could lose out on a move to Como, with Liverpool pricing the winger out of a switch. The Italian winger is expected to pursue a move away from Anfield this summer following a couple of frustrating seasons at the club.

‌



Having been signed from Italian giants Juventus, he has been limited to just 50 outings for the Reds due to injury and only nine of those have been starts.

‌



Chiesa continues to have admirers in Italy, including at Como, who are aiming to add to their squad having sealed a spot in the Champions League for next season.

‌



But it appears that a deal might not be so straightforward. Como president Mirwan Suwarso was asked about the chance of signing the winger but suggested that he could be too expensive.

Jurgen Klopp has already made Real Madrid feelings clear as fresh job offer 'sent' READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking to Tuttomercatoweb, he said: “We are looking at many players. The price for those players is a bit higher than the range we have in mind, though.”

‌



Chiesa, 28, has two years remaining on his contract with Liverpool but has suggested that talks will have to be held this summer regarding his future at the club.

He said: "If I don't find consistency in the Premier League, I'll have to look elsewhere. I barely played in my first year at Liverpool, and in the last one, very little.

"I'll go on a training camp in the US, then I'll talk to the club and the new manager, [Andoni] Iraola, and we'll see."

‌



View 2 Images Federico Chiesa has been linked with Cesc Fabregas' Como (Image: Getty Images)

"I've played very little since the start of 2026," the Italian added. "I have a great relationship with Liverpool. In January, the club and Slot told me I couldn't leave; they needed me, partly for numerical reasons.

"We were in a tight spot. I understood the situation and I was left smiling. Liverpool is always talked about; last year they helped me win the Premier League."

‌



Away from Chiesa, Liverpool might have a few other decisions to make when it comes to their squad this summer as Iraola attempts to reshape the team in his image.

Mohamed Salah and Andrew Robertson have already left the club at the end of their deals, the latter having signed a deal with Premier League rivals Tottenham Hotspur. Ibrahima Konate is also departing and is expected to join Spanish giants Real Madrid. Harvey Elliott could also leave following his disappointing loan spell with Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Arsenal make transfer move for PSG star who will be out of contract in days
Sports.content:
Arsenal make transfer move for PSG star who will be out of contract in days

Arsenal have made a move for a Paris Saint-Germain player who is set to be out of contract at the end of the June, as the Gunners look to get some transfer business in early

View 2 Images Arsenal are eyeing up a move for PSG's Emmanuel Mbemba (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal have made an approach to sign talented Paris St-Germain defender Emmanuel Mbemba on a free transfer this summer, it has been claimed.

‌



The 18-year-old has been offered a new contract by PSG but is open to a move to a top Premier League club, with training compensation set to be just over £150,000 after his contract expires at the end of June.

‌



According to the BBC, the Gunners have made 'contact' with Mbemba's representatives and outlined what the club could offer to him, making reference to William Saliba's progression when signed from Saint-Etienne.

‌



Erling Haaland to Real Madrid transfer row takes twist as response to statement issued READ MORE :

Thomas Frank makes decision on next job as ex-Tottenham boss speaks out READ MORE :

Saliba signed for Arsenal for £27million in 2019 and spent three years out on loan, first back at Saint-Etienne and then Nice and Marseille, before returning to Mikel Arteta's side for the 2022/23 season.

The Frenchman has since established a spot in Arsenal's first-choice XI alongside Gabriel Magalhaes at centre-back, making 184 appearances and helping the Gunners win the Premier League title this season.

Mbemba could replicate Saliba's progress and he is reported to 'favour' Arsenal, having seen the recent stability and success the team have had under manager Arteta's leadership across the last six years.

‌



View 2 Images Emmanuel Mbemba has been linked with a move to Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

During his chat with Arsenal, Mbemba was told he would go out on a European loan until January 2027, giving the 2008-born sensation time to seal a work permit to play in England.

While Mbemba has primarily played as a centre-back for PSG's Under 19s this season, the Gunners view him as a long-term option at left-back and succeeding Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie.

‌



Mbemba is a France youth international and has made 27 appearances for PSG's U19s this term, scoring twice. He was part of the PSG side that lost to Real Madrid in the semi-final of the UEFA Youth League.

Arsenal are expected to be active in the summer transfer window as they look to strengthen their squad after winning the Premier League title. Sandro Tonali, Eli Junior Kroupi and Julian Alvarez are among the players being linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium.

Sports.title: Epsom Derby punter backs winner thanks to discovery of 62-year-old buried time capsule
Sports.content:
Epsom Derby punter backs winner thanks to discovery of 62-year-old buried time capsule

A letter contained in the capsule found in Crystal Palace instructed the finder to put a bet on a runner with a Christmas-themed name in the Epsom Classic won by Christmas Day

View 2 Images A letter in a time capsule led the finder to put a bet on Christmas Day in the Derby

A construction worker is quids in after he took the advice of a letter discovered in a time capsule buried 62 years ago to back the winner of the Epsom Derby on Saturday.

‌



The discovery was made in April during building work at Crystal Palace Park in south London, which is undergoing a £22million regeneration. It was found underneath the bust of Sir Joseph Paxton, the Victorian garden designer who created the Crystal Palace, which was being removed to be relocated elsewhere on the site.

‌



The capsule contained a letter and some old English coins which had been the winnings from a bet placed on Santa Claus, winner of the Epsom Derby in 1964.

‌



Epsom Derby betting chaos after big favourite declared non-runner despite finishing race READ MORE :

Epsom Derby 2026 results in full as Christmas Day wins £2m race READ MORE :

Four shilling and two half crown coins, which would be the equivalent to about £10 today, were wrapped in a plastic sheet, along with a letter. The letter instructed the finder to use the money to bet on a horse with a name that could be "associated with 'Santa Claus'".

"Unbelievably, there is a horse in this year's Derby called Christmas Day," site manager Josh Smalls said. Smalls placed a £20 bet on Christmas Day, who went on the win the world famous horse races at a starting price of 7-1.

‌



He added: "It was very exciting. I was like a child on Christmas Day. To find a piece of history like that - and for it to link up so well with the horse this year - it was kind of spooky.

View 2 Images The note was found during the removal of a statue in Crystal Palace Park (Image: Jam Press/The Crystal Palace Park Trust)

"I looked through the rosters of the last few years and couldn't find any other horse with a Christmassy name."

Article continues below

Smalls said he grew up with horse racing: "My uncle was a racing horse trainer, I'd go to about two races every year. So this note sparked quite a bit of interest."

"Hopefully he'll win on Saturday and make everyone a bit of money," he added.

Bromley mayor Christine Harris also put £15 on Christmas Day with any winnings going to charity. After the race the Trust posted on Facebook, "What just happened?!?! The park’s time capsule prophecy came true. Christmas Day just won the Derby!"

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel sends Eberechi Eze message and gives heartbroken Arsenal stars reality check
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel says England’s players will “take care” of Eberechi Eze after his penalty shoot-out heartbreak.

Eze missed his spot kick in the Champions League final against Paris Saint Germain and it took Mikel Arteta to console him after Arsenal ’s devastating defeat.



Arsenal’s four players - Eze, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke and Declan Rice - have been given extra time off after the Champions League to recover both mentally and physically.

‌



It might hit Eze hardest of all because he missed from the spot in the shoot-out but Tuchel insists that his other players will ensure there is no hangover for the Arsenal players.

England boss Tuchel also reminded the Arsenal contingent that they have had a “great season” overall after winning the first title in 22 years and they matched the best club side in Europe in the Champions League final.

Thomas Tuchel gives England stars green light to complete blockbuster transfers READ MORE :

Tuchel said: “Of course it’s painful for Ebs but of course I will take care of it, the group will take care of him and I think the extra week they had will help a lot.

“I’m very happy that they got the title in England. I think that took a lot of weight off their shoulders and they were aware they did what they could and they were very close in the final.

‌



“I don’t think I will need to lift them. They’ve absolutely had a great season. I’m always happy to do it if I have to but they should know that a final just comes down to one or two shots in a penalty shoot-out which means it cannot be closer. At some point a winner has to be found.

“I have lost some finals in a penalty shoot-out and it’s the closest way to lose and it hurts of course, it hurts a lot to lose big finals but a penalty means you did evrything right, it couldn’t be closer.

View 3 Images Eze missed a penalty during the shootout defeat to PSG last weekend (Image: Getty Images)

“But it also means you were absolutely on the same level with maybe the best team in the world at the moment.”

‌



Arsenal’s four-strong contingent are flying in to West Palm Beach where England’ are training at the Palm Beach Gardens Tennis and Pickleball Centre.

But they are not expected to be at England’s first friendly against New Zealand which is 220 miles away in Tampa.

They will be reunited with their other England team mates when they return after the game and Tuchel has even arranged for them to be able to rewatch videos of team meetings which have been held this week.

Rice has played an exhausting amount of football while the others have also been on a rollercoaster ride after their season.

‌



Saka had a premiere of a new documentary on him in New York this week which Eze attended while the others took a break and Rice posted pictures of himself on his week off with Hollywood pal James Corden.

View 3 Images Declan Rice joined James Corden and ex-West Ham skipper James Corden

Tuchel expects the Arsenal players to be in great spirits and revealed that he has already been in touch with some of them to make them feel part of it.

Tuchel added: “I saw pictures and I heard messages already that they're happy to come, the group is waiting. We’re in good spirits, so this is normally what helps and I think they're very well aware of what they achieved this season.

‌



“I thought I would just leave them to themselves, so they could be proud of what they achieved. We spoke after their title in the Premier League, which was the big target and I think that was the main target.

"I could feel that it makes them proud, and took a weight off their shoulders and I think there is no need to be overly disappointed and to carry it into the World Cup campaign. I don't see that."

Sports.title: Man Utd star reveals Scott McTominay's true role in surprise World Cup call-up
Sports.content:
Man Utd star reveals Scott McTominay's true role in surprise World Cup call-up

Manchester United youngster Jack Fletcher has been included in Scotland’s squad for the World Cup following an injury to Billy Gilmour and he has praised a former Red Devils teammate

View 2 Images Scott McTomimay will represent Scotland at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Jack Fletcher has praised Scott McTominay for his help following his surprise World Cup call-up. The Manchester United youngster has been named as a late inclusion in Scotland’s squad for the upcoming tournament.

‌



He was called up by Steve Clarke after Billy Gilmour’s injury saw his hopes of playing at the World Cup ended. And Fletcher has now given an insight into his rollercoaster week, and hailed McTominay for his help in getting integrated into the squad.

‌



He said: “It’s been a crazy week! I didn’t really expect it but I am just taking it in my stride and loving every minute of it so far. In the changing room, after I found out Billy [Gilmour] got injured and I was obviously gutted for him.

‌



“The manager come up to me and said ‘I might not be the last time I see you on this trip’. I was a bit like: ‘Wow’. Then, the next morning, I got a call saying do you want to go to the World Cup.

FIFA forced into another humbling U-turn days before 2026 World Cup kicks off READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel gives England stars green light to complete blockbuster transfers READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“I was speechless and obviously said yes! I’ve got nothing with me, I’ve got nothing in my suitcase. I’ve got no boots, I am getting my boots sent over today actually.

‌



“It was in the back of my head that if I go and make an impression. I could go and make it into the first team and be around it. But to go to the World Cup a week after training is something I never thought of it or could of dreamed of.

“I knew Scott [McTominay] from United, he has helped me a lot. Kenny McLean has been top with me a – really top guy. One of the best players I have ever trained with, he is so good, all of them are and it is a great team to be around.”

View 2 Images Jack Fletcher has surprisingly been called up into Scotland's World Cup squad (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Fletcher, 19, is the son of ex-United midfielder Darren Fletcher and a product of the United academy. He has gone on to make three first-team appearances for the club. He had previously progressed through the England youth ranks but eventually chose to represent Scotland on the international stage.

Scotland take on Bolivia in their final warm-up game on Sunday before attention will then turn to the World Cup itself. Clarke’s side will clash with Haiti, Morocco and Brazil in Group C.

The nation’s appearance at the World Cup represents their first in nearly 30 years. They have never managed to qualify out of the group.

Sports.title: West Ham star sends message to David Sullivan after he steps down over 'historic allegations'
Sports.content:
West Ham star sends message to David Sullivan after he steps down over 'historic allegations'

David Sullivan has stepped down from his role as joint-chairman and director of West Ham after being made aware of the impending publication of 'serious historic allegations' which he denies

View 2 Images David Sullivan has stepped down as joint-chairman of West Ham (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

West Ham midfielder Mohamadou Kante has issued a statement in support of David Sullivan after he stepped down as the club's joint-chairman and director.

‌



Sullivan took the decision on Saturday after being made aware of the impending publication of 'serious historic allegations' which he denies.

‌



West Ham said in a statement: "It is understood none of the allegations relate to West Ham United or any of its operations.

‌



"Through his own legal representatives Mr Sullivan denies any illegal conduct and has taken the decision to step down in order to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately."

The 77-year-old had held the role of joint-chairman at West Ham for 16 years, having completed a takeover of the club in 2010 alongside his former business partner David Gold.

Kante joined West Ham from Paris FC in August 2024 on a five-year contract. The 20-year-old has made 14 appearances for the first team so far and has decided to speak out in support of Sullivan.

‌



"In a period like this, I wanted to send a personal message to David Sullivan," the Frenchman wrote on Instagram. "When I went through difficult times at the beginning of my career, he was one of the few people to trust me. He believed in me, supported me with patience and respect, and it meant a lot to me.

View 2 Images Mohamadou Kante has posted a statement in support of David Sullivan (Image: Getty Images)

"I can only talk about the man I knew and the help he gave me at an important moment in my life. I respect the work of justice and I have confidence that the truth will be established by the competent authorities.

‌



"In anticipation of this, I simply wanted to show him my human support and tell him that my thoughts are with him and his family in this particularly difficult time."

In a statement, Sullivan said: "I have recently become aware that factually incorrect and entirely false, decades-old allegations concerning my personal life are due to be broadcast and published. The false allegations levelled against me have been sensationalised by the media.

"After a lifetime spent building businesses in the adult industry in which I have met thousands of women, it is sadly inevitable that a small number of improper conduct claims are being made against me. I categorically deny these claims. I am a private man, and those who personally and professionally know the real David Sullivan, not the caricature invented by the tabloids, know exactly who I am and what I stand for. I am absolutely not the person the media has decided to paint me as.

Article continues below

"I have not been provided with any proper explanation as to how these individuals or their claims were independently verified or assessed for credibility prior to publication. I believe that the entire process has been fundamentally unfair and completely lacking in any due impartiality."

Sports.title: Epsom Derby betting chaos after big favourite declared non-runner despite finishing race
Sports.content:
Epsom Derby betting chaos after big favourite declared non-runner despite finishing race

Benvenuto Cellini went off as the 3-1 favourite for the £2million race but never featured after starting slowly and trailing behind stablemate Christmas Day

View 3 Images Benvenuto Ceillini's hind leg was trapped on the running board

The Betfred Derby market was plunged into chaos on Saturday after the big race favourite was declared a non-runner - despite finishing the race.

‌



Benvenuto Cellini, one of four colts trained by Aidan O’Brien, went off at odds of 3-1 under Ryan Moore to win the £2million historic Classic at Epsom. But he broke very slowly, had only one horse behind him descending Tattenham Corner and never featured, trailing in well adrift of winning stablemate Christmas Day.

‌



A stewards inquiry was announced when officials looked into the reasons for Benvenuto Cellini’s slow start. Cameras in the starting stalls revealed that Benvenuto Cellini had his left hind leg stuck on the running board and so exited the structure on three legs.

‌



Epsom Derby 2026 results in full as Christmas Day wins £2m race READ MORE :

Laura Pearson outfoxes rivals to land Derby day win at track where she broke her neck READ MORE :

The hearing considered whether the colt was denied a fair start and as Moore stated he had wanted to race more forward, it was decided he was negatively impacted.

The stewards announced he was a non-runner which resulted in a Rule 4 being declared for betting purposes. It meant all stakes on Benvenuto Cellini were refunded and 25p in the pound was deducted from winnings on Christmas Day.

Bookmaker Jerry White, operating from the Kalooki Racing pitch in the Epsom betting ring, said: “You couldn’t make it up, could you?

‌



View 3 Images Benvenuto Cellini (circled) finished down the field but was declared a non-runner

“Something always goes wrong in life but today of all the big stages you wouldn’t want it to happen the Derby favourite is deemed to be a non-runner.

“If you backed it you get your money back. If you backed the winner Christmas Day then you get a 25p in the pound deduction from the winnings.

‌



“For us it was a shocking result as we’ve got to give all the money back on the favourite and we’ve still got to pay all the punters who backed Christmas Day.”

However, a number of high street bookies decided to waive the Rule 4 and not make the deduction, including Coral, Ladbrokes and Boyle Sports, as a goodwill gesture.

"Christmas Day was an apt winner of a Derby that was run in wintry conditions, conditions that very much suited Ronan Whelan's mount, with punters backing him at all rates from 16-1 down to 7-1, so it was not an unpopular victory by any means," said Coral's David Stevens.

‌



View 3 Images Christmas Day: bookmakers waived the Rule 4 deduction (Image: Getty Images)

"Benvenuto Cellini was sent off favourite, or at least he would have been had he not been deemed a non-runner, but as a goodwill gesture to our customers, we are waiving the Rule 4 deduction on him, so that winning punters do not lose out on the biggest betting race of the Flat season.”

Chief stipendiary steward Shaun Parker explained: “Soon after the horses had left the starting gates we were notified that the favourite had his left hind leg on the running board, just before the start was affected and as the start was affected which resulted in him not being able to jump on terms with the field, as he was standing on three legs when the stalls opened.

Article continues below

“We then considered the fact in terms of our rules whether he had been denied a fair start. Having got evidence from Ryan Moore importantly in terms of what the instructions were and where he actually wanted to be in terms of the race.

“He wanted to go forward with the horse. We noticed he was very slow into stride and was second last shortly after the start and really on the back foot. His race was in our view negatively affected. On that basis we can then declare the horse a non-runner.”
